links.comparator_used: AI model predictions shown without image-based explanations (saliency heatmaps)
links.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy for pneumonia, heart failure and COPD, with systematically biased AI predictions
links.effect: Biased predictions with explanations decreased accuracy by 9.1 percentage points (95% CI, 4.9 to 13.2) vs baseline; biased predictions without explanations decreased it by 11.3 points (95% CI, 7.2 to 15.5); nonsignificant improvement of 2.3 points (95% CI, -2.7 to 7.2). For standard models, explanations raised accuracy by 4.4 points (95% CI, 2.0 to 6.9) vs 2.9 points (95% CI, 0.5 to 5.2) without.
links.tradeoff: Explanations did not mitigate the harm from systematically biased models; clinician accuracy still fell well below baseline.
links.quote: Systematically biased AI model predictions decreased clinician accuracy by 11.3 percentage points (95% CI, 7.2 to 15.5) compared with baseline and providing biased AI model predictions with explanations decreased clinician accuracy by 9.1 percentage points (95% CI, 4.9 to 13.2) compared with baseline, representing a nonsignificant improvement of 2.3 percentage points (95% CI, -2.7 to 7.2) compared with the systematically biased AI model.
